observations.body: David strikes the Amalekites, recovers every person and possession, rejects exclusion of those who stayed with the baggage, and sends gifts to Judah’s elders.
observations.label: Recovery becomes a rule about sharing: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, four hundred fighters, two hundred who remain, families, Amalekites, and Judah’s elders, the Amalekite camp, Besor, and towns of Judah, attacking, recovering, disputing, sharing, legislating, and sending gifts visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Recovery becomes a rule about sharing: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: David, four hundred fighters, two hundred who remain, families, Amalekites, and Judah’s elders · the Amalekite camp, Besor, and towns of Judah · attacking, recovering, disputing, sharing, legislating, and sending gifts · restoration becomes a distribution rule and renewed relation with Judah
observations.label: Relationships named in 1 Samuel 30:16–31

payload.posture: Read 1 Samuel 30:16–31 as its own philistine brink and recovery David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places restoration becomes a distribution rule and renewed relation with Judah inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: Recovery becomes a rule about sharing
